fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
the Ember 8 flagship rate was 9.9 per 100,000

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents initially reported by a customer or installer. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their unit or a materially similar model, with immediate instructions for safe operation.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved representative sample and published test protocol. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. A model exceeding that rate must promptly submit corrective actions and a passing-retest plan to the regulator. The regulator may authorize time-limited continued sales subject to risk-based conditions, customer protections, and defined milestones where appropriate; otherwise, new placements must pause until corrective action and a passing retest are completed. Complete current per-model test methods, sample sizes, failure rates, and results must be provided to customers and prospective customers of that model in an accessible format, and updated when material information changes.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the customer and, where an imminent hazard warrants it, by the manufacturer or emergency responders, with appropriate safeguards against unauthorized activation. Existing installed systems must be retrofitted or replaced to provide this capability within six years of the standard’s effective date, unless a documented technical impossibility is accepted by the regulator; interim risk controls and customer instructions are required.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after this standard’s adoption must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of fire propagation. Manufacturers must provide regulators with the design basis and validation evidence.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall of a model when its thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, using regulator-validated incident and installed-unit counts. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers promptly and provide safe-use instructions and a remedy; the regulator may require a broader or faster recall where warranted.

document.section_notes: S1 imposes strict 24-hour reporting for all incidents and 48-hour customer notice, with reporting required regardless of cause confirmation. S2 sets a 55 °C test and 5% permanent failure limit, allows regulator-authorized time-limited continued sales for noncompliant models, and requires per-model numeric results to customers but not public publication. S3 requires remote shut-off on new units and a 6-year retrofit deadline with a technical-impossibility exception; S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8 incidents/100k with prompt customer notices but no explicit serious-injury clause.
